slot.brief: Rank given haloalkanes by SN1 rate, driven by carbocation stability (including a resonance-stabilised arylmethyl case).

stem: In the same polar protic solvent, arrange these haloalkanes in increasing order of their $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction rates: chloroethane, 2-chloropropane and benzyl chloride.

verdicts.working: SN1 rate follows carbocation stability: primary ethyl < secondary isopropyl < resonance-stabilized benzyl. Thus chloroethane < 2-chloropropane < benzyl chloride.

working:
$\text{S}_\text{N}1$ rate increases with carbocation stability.
Ethyl cation $<$ isopropyl cation; the benzyl cation is resonance-stabilised.
Thus: chloroethane $<$ 2-chloropropane $<$ benzyl chloride.

Independent check: SN1 rate follows carbocation stability: primary ethyl < secondary isopropyl < resonance-stabilized benzyl. Thus chloroethane < 2-chloropropane < benzyl chloride.
solution:
The $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ rate increases with the stability of the carbocation formed in the rate-determining step.
$$\text{ethyl}^+ < \text{isopropyl}^+ < \text{benzyl}^+$$
The benzyl carbocation is resonance-stabilized; hence, chloroethane $<$ 2-chloropropane $<$ benzyl chloride.
